# ForgeOS v0.6 Benchmark Methodology

The v0.6 benchmarks are reproducible release regressions. They are not universal comparisons against unrelated projects.

The release evaluates the current 128-technique Skill Intelligence kernel and its deterministic execution surfaces without treating the 1,024 outcome scaffolds as deep skills.

## Router benchmark

The pinned corpus measures Precision@1, Precision@3, Recall@6, unsafe/quarantined activation, deterministic replay, exclusion explanations, anti-trigger behavior, and cross-outcome composition. Current public results are P@1 93.75%, P@3 100%, Recall@6 100%, unsafe activation 0%, and determinism 100%. Results apply only to the published corpus and source revision.

## Context benchmark

The context corpus checks 33/33 stable provider materialization, one accounting boundary between resolver/materializer, request-wide budget enforcement, omission manifests, large-log distillation, and Semantic ABI orientation reduction. It does not prove every hosted model tokenizer has p95 error below 8%; real usage receipts remain necessary for that claim.

## Code Review Intelligence

The bundled 12-case corpus measures deterministic scope coverage, work-unit bundling, contextual rules, anchor validity/relocation, reflection noise filtering, and receipt completeness. It is a conformance vertical slice, not the proposed expert-adjudicated benchmark of 50+ repositories, 200+ PRs, ten languages, and 1,500 issues.

## Security and federation

The Agent Surface Security corpus currently has 20 cases; the federation adversarial corpus has 18. Both are deterministic release blockers. Passing them does not imply immunity to unknown attack classes.

## Comparison claims

ForgeOS may claim superiority on a metric only when the baseline version, tasks, seeds, models, hardware, cost, raw evidence, confidence, and failure cases are public and identical. Stars and repository popularity are not benchmark evidence.
